# Global cut partitions for the ambient transfer

Machine-authored live request a27f6d422b1a478c976694b9ca5c9a54. No novelty
claim. Full published Conjecture63 remains unresolved. Only final successful
validation receipts count as formal evidence.

For a word w, use the inherited positive ambient transfer
T_r=D_r+x c_r H, where H=(1,1)^T(y,1), c_A=1, c_B=1+y,
D_A=[[0,0],[0,1]], and D_B=[[y,0],[2y,1]]. Append one B to w.
The inherited scalar is exactly (y,1) T_(wB) (0,1)^T.

The first row (p,q) has two possible transitions at a position:

* Skip: (p,q)D_A=(0,q), or (p,q)D_B=(y(p+2q),q).
* Select: multiply by x c_r(p+q), then reset the row to (y,1).

Let C(y,p,q;w;s) count exactly s selected positions with these weights.
For the empty word C(0)=q and C(s+1)=0. At r followed by v,

    C(y,p,q;rv;0)=C(y,d_r(p,q),q;v;0),
    C(y,p,q;rv;s+1)=C(y,d_r(p,q),q;v;s+1)
                    +c_r(p+q) C(y,y,1;v;s).

MarkovCutPartitionA27 proves universally that this is the ordinary x
coefficient of the transfer scalar. It proves the zero count C(...;0)=q,
vanishing above the word length, and scalar nonnegativity for nonnegative
real inputs. The latter is explicitly scalar nonnegativity, not an assertion
that pointwise positivity alone implies coefficientwise positivity.

For every actual source path, every natural i,j,s with i+j=a+s, the checked
bridge is

    A(i,j)=[y^j] C(y,y,1;central(path) B;s).

There is no cutoff, normalization, specialization y=1, or suppressed zero.
MarkovCutRootA27 extends this to every original grid position by returning zero
when i+j<a, and proves this is the actual raw coefficient there too. Its
root_iff_cutA27 is an exact equivalence with all three original inequalities
and their three polygon guards. Neither side of this equivalence is proved.

## Explicit gap weights

Write p_u for the first row entry after skipping a gap u, starting at (y,1),
and R(u)=p_u+1. Selecting positions k_1<...<k_s in wB contributes the product
of c_(k_h) R(gap_h); the unselected suffix after the last position contributes
1. For zero selected positions the contribution is 1. This subset description
is the direct expansion of the checked select/skip recursion. The explicit
finite-subset sum is independently tested in Python; it is not a separately
formalized Finset identity.

The universally checked gap formulas are

    R(B^q)=1+2(y+...+y^q)+y^(q+1),
    R(u A B^q)=1+2(y+...+y^q).

Thus a gap weight depends only on its trailing B run and whether the gap is
pure B. In particular its coefficient list is [1,2,...,2,1] or [1,2,...,2].
The q=0 cases are included: the empty gap has weight 1+y, and a gap ending
in A has weight 1. MarkovCutGapsA27 proves these over every commutative ring.

There is no uniform sign for splitting a gap. If alpha_v is the skipped
first-state output starting at (1,0), and beta_v that starting at (0,1),
the checked identity is

    R(u)R(v)-(1+y)R(uv)=(p_u-y)(1+beta_v-alpha_v).

For u=v=A this equals -y; for u=B,v=A it equals y+y^2. This rules out both
unconditional signs for this particular local split comparison, without
refuting a global sum inequality or a source-specific comparison.

# Exact lower-corner results and summation obstructions

Machine-authored research, request 3979f3c739b946f2a07319e5c9795bce.
Full pinned Conjecture63 remains unresolved. No historical novelty claim.

For every n>=0 take the actual source at (n+2)/(n+3), namely the protected
frame at replicate(n+1,true), and its vertical raw triple starting at (n+2,0).
The checked formulas in MarkovPellMixture3979 are

    A(n+2,0) = 1,
    A(n+2,1) = 3n+5,
    A(n+2,2) = (17n²+23n+12)/2.

All three positions belong to the pinned polygon. The formulas derive from
the inherited all-coordinate excess identity, with natural-subtraction and
zero cases retained. Rational casts in the proof do not change coefficients.
The raw log-concavity gap is (n²+37n+38)/2, hence positive. A separate base
case also covers source 1/2, whose right endpoint coefficient is zero.
`excess_vertical_zero3979` establishes the whole s=0 case of the inherited
ExcessVertical00b3 predicate; when j>0 its left endpoint is zero.

The same literal source triples give an infinite obstruction to averaging
across source labels. Sum the triples for n=0,...,N-1 without weights or
normalization. Their sums are

    N, (3N²+7N)/2, (17N³+9N²+10N)/6.

Twelve times (endpoint product minus center square) equals

    N² (7N²-108N-127).

`bottom_sum_lc_iff3979` proves that the aggregate is log-concave exactly for
N<=16. Every N>=17 reverses the inequality, despite every summand being a
valid source triple satisfying it. At N=17 the aggregate is [17,493,14382],
and the reversed gap is 1445. Aggregating different source polynomials is
not an operation in Conjecture63, so this is a strategy obstruction only.

## The geometric-convolution obstruction

Let E_s be the already source-connected Pell excess series

    (x+y)^(2s) / ((1-x)^(s+1) (1-y)^s).

The new kernel module defines F_s=E_s/(1-x) using the actual formal power
series product. `prefix_coeff_sum3979` proves its coefficient is exactly the
finite prefix sum of E_s coefficients, without dropping zeros. At the three
cross-strip positions (s,i,j)=(0,10,0),(1,10,1),(2,10,2), its coefficients
are [11,155,2202]. The checked strict inequality is 155²<11*2202.
`zero_slice_preservation_failure3979` also proves that E_s satisfies every
input comparison on this zero-excess vertical slice, whereas F_s does not.
Thus preserving this slice under an extra positive geometric factor is false.
This does not refute a preservation theorem whose stronger input hypotheses
have not been established. F_s is not identified with a source family.

## Experimental directions retained

The generalized kernel probe considered
(x+y)^(2s)/(1-x)^(s+p)/(1-y)^(s+q). It made 129600 exact comparisons for
p,q<=5, s<=8, i,j<=19. The first horizontal failure is p=0,q=2,s=0,i=0,j=10,
with [11,155,2202], the transpose of the formal witness above. This rules out
that unrestricted deformation, not the p=1,q=0 source case.

Exact rational polynomial expansion tested the horizontal and vertical gaps
for positive excess s=1,...,6. After the same safe interior translations as
the inherited first-band proof, every monomial coefficient was nonnegative.
This suggests investigating a uniform symbolic certificate. No theorem for
arbitrary s, or for excluded boundary coordinates, follows from these tests.

The arbitrary A--core--B horizontal-only conjecture survived 951 additional
structured and deterministically randomized words, with a 55-second cap.
The exact generator and seed 3979 are saved. These words are an enlarged
family; the scan proves neither their horizontal conjecture nor the root.

One useful interpretation of the inherited horizontal sum is a colored
monomer-dimer model. For an alternating path of 2a vertices (2a-1 edges), give
even-position edges weight 1 and odd-position edges weight ty. A matching
with a-s dimers leaves 2s free vertices, each carrying weight 1+y. The number
with q odd dimers is choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q), for positive s. Thus its
coefficient of t^q y^j is exactly H(a,j,s,q) from the inherited fiber goal.
The binomial count follows from the inherited matching-coefficient formula
with indices (a-s-q,q); out-of-range cases need their explicit guards.
This is an explanatory representation, not a new formal combinatorial
injection. A comparison at fixed charge j remains unproved. The cumulative
counterexample cautions against replacing that comparison by free summation.

Live literature queries revisited the [published target](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html)
and located [Mu--Zheng's Delannoy matrix study](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0013091522000384),
[Foldes--Major's Pascal-type triangle paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.04126),
and [Zhu's Riordan-array paper](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/2121C9E7369DEC3D5C05B2C6735165E3/S0308210516000500a.pdf/logconcavity_and_strong_qlogconvexity_for_riordan_arrays_and_recursive_matrices.pdf).
No applicable theorem with all hypotheses verified was obtained. This was
not an exhaustive survey; no retrieved statement was imported as a Lean axiom.
# Centered horizontal fibers and LC-positivity

Machine-authored research, request 65c4dfb883e140b0a62fddbffe247137.
The full pinned Conjecture63 remains open. No historical novelty is claimed.
Formal validation status is recorded separately in the final validation manifest.

Use the inherited, source-connected horizontal summands

    H(a,j,s,q) = choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) choose(2s,j-q), s>0.

Out-of-range terms are zero. The inherited Lean horizontalTerm uses s-1.
For a fixed combined index k, pair the terms q and k-q in the coefficient of
F_s(t)^2-F_(s-1)(t)F_(s+1)(t). For q<k/2 the signed layer is

    D_q = 2 H_s(q)H_s(k-q)
          -H_(s-1)(q)H_(s+1)(k-q)-H_(s+1)(q)H_(s-1)(k-q).

For 2q=k use H_s(q)^2-H_(s-1)(q)H_(s+1)(q). Retain zeros.
The candidate condition is that every centered tail sum, from r to floor(k/2),
is nonnegative. This is equivalent, by grouping the two convolution orders,
to coefficientwise log-concavity after cutting off every q<r in each F_s.
The exact unsymmetrized convolution identity is formalized in
MarkovTruncatedFiber65c4; the regrouping equivalence in this paragraph is an
elementary paper derivation, not claimed as a separately checked Lean theorem.

This is the LC-positivity framework of Wang--Yeh. Their finite Abel argument
weights signed layers by a nonnegative increasing sequence. For a nonnegative
CrossLC sequence f, the centered products f(q)f(k-q) increase up to the center.
MarkovAbel65c4 checks this finite-sum transfer, including zero weights. Its tail
inequalities remain explicit hypotheses. They are NOT established for all H.
The source transfer from the new truncated-fiber proposition to every Pell
horizontal polygon triple is formalized using the inherited exact bridge.
It still has the truncated-fiber proposition as an unproved premise.

## Exact experiments

pair-probe.json covers all a=3,...,35, 0<=j<=2a, 1<=s<a and
0<=k<=2(a-s). There are 286187 nonzero fibers. All tested centered tails
are nonnegative; after removing zero layers the signs never change from
positive back to negative. At a=3,j=2,s=2,k=2, the layers are [-15,64].
Thus nonnegativity of individual layers is false, while their sum is 49.
The concrete layers and all cutoffs of that fiber are checked in Lean.

pair-random.json records seed 6504, 1500 trials and 703 nonzero fibers with
a<=499, again without a centered-tail or sign-order failure. These are finite
exact experiments and supply no universal statement.

pair-polynomial.json makes a different test. For each s=1,...,8, k=0,...,18
and 0<=j<=2(s+1)+k, replace a by s+k+1+X. Every binomial depending on a is
expanded as its falling-factorial polynomial over Q. This shift puts all
q<=k in the ordinary nonnegative-binomial range. All 19080 centered tails
have nonnegative ordinary X coefficients. This is finite symbolic evidence
for a stronger positivity candidate. It leaves arbitrary s,k and the region
a<s+k+1 unresolved. It is not a proof of universal coefficient positivity.

## A uniform refined fiber

For a=m+3, j=2, center excess s=2 and combined index k=2, write O(m) for
the outer layer and C(m) for the center layer. Direct binomial algebra gives

    2(O(m)+C(m)) = 31m^4+199m^3+435m^2+365m+98.

C(m)>=0 follows from the already proved individual-summand inequality.
Hence both centered tails are nonnegative for every m>=0. For any real
x,z>=0 and xz<=y^2, O(m)xz+C(m)y^2>=0. This is an unbounded parameter
certificate for ONE refined fiber, not for all fibers or the Markov goal.
MarkovFiberPolynomial65c4 checks the identity, positivity and weighted
inequality. It compiled and kernel-replayed successfully; the source hashes
and receipts are in the validation manifest. Its imports reuse inherited
compiled artifacts, rather than a fresh whole-source rebuild.

## Sources and applicability

[Wang--Yeh, Log-concavity and LC-positivity](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0504164v7),
Lemma 2.1 and Section 2, supplies the finite Abel framework and interpretation
of truncated coefficient arrays. Our array also depends on fixed a and j;
their results do not automatically prove its required tail inequalities.

[Chen--Sun, fan coordinates of type A_n](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.09312v1)
treats laminar interval products and the particular exponent map
L(k)=(k1+k2,...,kn+k(n+1)). No identification of this map with the pinned
Markov coefficient fibers was obtained. Its theorem is not imported or applied.

The [published Markov target](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html)
was retrieved live. No source statement is introduced as a Lean axiom.
# Exact Pell sums and a directional pair-fiber conjecture

Machine-authored request 9a720f77696445aab32325da611c5097.
The full pinned Conjecture63 remains unresolved. This report makes no
historical novelty claim. Final formal status is in
evidence/markov-9a720f77/validation.json.

Write a=n+1 for the numerator of the source (n+1)/(n+2), and d=2a.
For every natural i,j with a<=i+j<=2a put r=2a-i-j. The new theorem proves

    A(i,j) = sum over 0<=k<=i and k<=r of
        choose(2a-2r,i-k) choose(a-r+k,k) choose(a-k-1,r-k).

Natural subtraction is used in Lean. Outside the degree strip the expression
is zero. The proof uses literal quotient coefficients and ordinary polynomial
multiplication, and proves the outside-strip zero cases separately. It retains
every raw coefficient and has no denominator cutoff. Together with the prior
diagonal theorem, WeakLC for the entire Pell family is equivalent to the two
horizontal/vertical inequalities for this explicit sum. Both remain unproved.

For positive excess degree i+j=a+s, s>=1, a reindexing gives

    A(i,j) = sum_q H(a,j,s,q),
    H(a,j,s,q) = choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) choose(2s,j-q).

Terms with q>j are zero, as are the out-of-range binomial terms. The formal
horizontalTerm9a72 uses parameter s-1, avoiding negative natural upper indices.
right_horizontal_sum_fixed9a72 proves this identity with the fixed range
0<=q<=a, with all zero terms retained. horizontal_term_lc9a72 proves every
individual summand log-concave as s varies through positive integers. Its proof
uses fixed-upper binomial LC, upper-index binomial LC at stride one and stride
two, and multiplication of nonnegative LC triples. This does not prove the sum
LC; the missing closure is explicitly retained.

## New experimental candidate and its exact formal transfer

Let F_s(t)=sum_q H(a,j,s,q)t^q. The candidate is coefficientwise

    F_(s+1)(t)^2 - F_s(t) F_(s+2)(t) >= 0.

HorizontalFiberGoal9a72 states the corresponding precise bounded-parameter
claim. Evaluating at t=1 would give the raw horizontal inequality.
source_near_one_horizontal_of_fiber9a72 proves that implication for every
actual source path with b=a+1. The j=0 boundary is already proved and is handled
separately. For j>0 the polygon bounds ensure the positive-excess formulas
apply at all three positions. Thus the conditional transfer has no missing
coefficient or zero-support premise. The fiber goal itself is NOT proved.

The complete finite scan through a=50 tested both horizontal and vertical
analogues: 169,050 parameter triples and 2,266,833 nonzero endpoint fibers.
No horizontal failure occurred. The vertical analogue fails at a=10,i=10,
center excess s=1 and combined summand index 16: there are 84 endpoint pairs
but only 81 center pairs. The unrefined raw triple is 1,29,642 and satisfies
the pinned inequality. A further 1,200 deterministic horizontal trials with
a<=250 checked 50,506 nonzero fibers and found no failure. These are finite
experiments, not proofs. Inputs and outputs are saved under evidence/markov-9a720f77/.

There is a potentially useful formal-power-series expression behind H:

    sum_q choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) x^q
      = [z^(a-s)] (1-z)^(-s-1) (1-x*z)^(-s).

This follows by the two negative-binomial expansions. It is a research
derivation, not a new Lean theorem. Combining it with (1+y)^(2s) recovers the
j-refinement. A possible next direction is proving coefficientwise LC through
this generating function or a planar path model; no such proof is asserted.

## Rejected stronger approaches

Termwise midpoint balancing and pairwise synchronization both fail for H.
The exact inequalities are checked in MarkovPellObstructions9a72. Those
failures do not rule out aggregate conservation of the combined index q+r.
The separate vertical decomposition fails even that aggregate condition.

For actual source 3/4, the vertical slice i=3 is [1,8,26,20]. The formal
normalization obstruction is 8^2<3*1*26; the raw inequalities still hold.
Exact rational Sturm experiments on 966 nonzero Pell horizontal/vertical
slices find non-real roots, including this cubic and a horizontal slice at
7/8. The Sturm implementation is experimental evidence, not a Lean theorem.

The interrupted predecessor was reconciled from its raw event log: its final
manifest and report were saved after all six successful replays. No prior
side effect was blindly repeated. Construction and Agoh were left untouched.

/-! Machine-authored a27f6d42. Closed run weights and exact cut-insertion defect. -/
namespace MathGKM.Markov
noncomputable section

def gapChargeA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y p q : R) : List Bool → R
 | [] => p
 | r::rs => gapChargeA27 y (cutChargeA27 y p q r) q rs

theorem gapCharge_appendA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y p q : R)
 (u v : List Bool) : gapChargeA27 y p q (u++v)=
 gapChargeA27 y (gapChargeA27 y p q u) q v := by
 induction u generalizing p with
 | nil => rfl
 | cons r rs ih => simpa only [List.cons_append,gapChargeA27] using ih _

def runSumA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y : R) (n : ℕ) : R :=
 ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, y^(k+1)

theorem runSum_succA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y : R) (n : ℕ) :
 runSumA27 y (n+1)=y*(runSumA27 y n+1) := by
 rw [runSumA27,Finset.sum_range_succ']
 simp only [Nat.zero_add,pow_one,runSumA27,mul_add,mul_one,Finset.mul_sum]
 congr 1
 apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
 intro k hk
 ring

theorem gapCharge_runA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y p q : R) (n : ℕ) :
 gapChargeA27 y p q (List.replicate n true)=y^n*p+2*q*runSumA27 y n := by
 induction n generalizing p with
 | zero => simp [gapChargeA27,runSumA27]
 | succ n ih =>
   rw [List.replicate_succ',gapCharge_appendA27]
   simp only [gapChargeA27,cutChargeA27,if_true]
   rw [ih,runSum_succA27,pow_succ]
   ring

def gapWeightA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y : R) (w : List Bool) : R :=
 gapChargeA27 y y 1 w+1

theorem gapWeight_pureA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y : R) (n : ℕ) :
 gapWeightA27 y (List.replicate n true)=1+2*runSumA27 y n+y^(n+1) := by
 rw [gapWeightA27,gapCharge_runA27]
 ring

theorem gapWeight_resetA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y : R)
 (u : List Bool) (n : ℕ) :
 gapWeightA27 y (u++false::List.replicate n true)=1+2*runSumA27 y n := by
 rw [gapWeightA27,gapCharge_appendA27,gapChargeA27]
 simp [cutChargeA27,gapCharge_runA27,add_comm]

/-- Every gap map is affine in its incoming first state, preserving q. -/
theorem gapCharge_affineA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y p q : R)
 (w : List Bool) :
 gapChargeA27 y p q w =
 p*gapChargeA27 y 1 0 w+q*gapChargeA27 y 0 1 w := by
 induction w generalizing p q with
 | nil => simp [gapChargeA27]
 | cons r rs ih =>
   simp only [gapChargeA27]
   rw [ih (cutChargeA27 y p q r) q, ih (cutChargeA27 y 1 0 r) 0,
     ih (cutChargeA27 y 0 1 r) 1]
   cases r <;> simp [cutChargeA27] <;> ring

/-- Splitting a gap has no uniform sign, even though each weight is positive. -/
theorem gapWeight_splitA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y : R)
 (u v : List Bool) :
 gapWeightA27 y u*gapWeightA27 y v-(1+y)*gapWeightA27 y (u++v)=
 (gapChargeA27 y y 1 u-y)*
   (1+gapChargeA27 y 0 1 v-gapChargeA27 y 1 0 v) := by
 simp only [gapWeightA27,gapCharge_appendA27]
 rw [gapCharge_affineA27 y (gapChargeA27 y y 1 u) 1 v,
   gapCharge_affineA27 y y 1 v]
 ring

theorem gapWeight_split_falseA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y : R) :
 gapWeightA27 y [false]*gapWeightA27 y [false] -
   (1+y)*gapWeightA27 y [false,false] = -y := by
 simp [gapWeightA27,gapChargeA27,cutChargeA27] <;> ring

theorem gapWeight_split_true_falseA27 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (y : R) :
 gapWeightA27 y [true]*gapWeightA27 y [false] -
   (1+y)*gapWeightA27 y [true,false] = y+y^2 := by
 simp [gapWeightA27,gapChargeA27,cutChargeA27] <;> ring

#print axioms gapWeight_pureA27
#print axioms gapWeight_resetA27
#print axioms gapWeight_splitA27
#print axioms gapWeight_split_falseA27
#print axioms gapWeight_split_true_falseA27
end

theorem ambient_word_appendB5 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (x y : R)
 (w z : List Bool) :
 ambientWord5c x y (w++z)=mm16 (ambientWord5c x y w) (ambientWord5c x y z) := by
 induction w with

 | cons r rs ih => simp only [List.cons_append,ambientWord5c,ih,mm_assoc16]

theorem ambient_quad_sandwichB5 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (x y p q : R)
 (w : List Bool) (r : Bool) :

two factors, scalars compensate a possible failure of individual log-concavity.

Write L_i=H(a,j,s,q+i), M_i=H(a,j,s+1,q+i), R_i=H(a,j,s+2,q+i).

# Second horizontal row

Machine-authored research, 2026-10-14; request 8934af1772f94a59862d7005ebd43159.
Full Conjecture 6.3 remains open. This is not an independent completion audit.

For an arbitrary word A w B, let n=length(w), m=count_B(w). When w is
nonempty, let f and r indicate that its first and last letters are B, and
let k count adjacent BB pairs inside w. Put s=f+r+2k. The exact formula for
n>=3 is

    2 [v²]P = u^m (1+u)^(n-3) Q(u),
    Q(u) = 4s + (9m²+13m+6)u
         + (6m²+6mn+8m+6n+6)u²
         + (m+n+2)(m+n+1)u³.

There is also a denominator-cleared identity valid for every nonempty core:
multiply the second coefficient by 2(1+u)^3 and the cubic by u^m(1+u)^n.
The formula is proved by a second-order coefficient invariant of the literal
positive matrix recurrence, over arbitrary commutative rings. In particular,
the order-dependent constant is not replaced by a conjectured count formula.
An induction proves 0<=s<=2m.

For actual source words, a=m+1 and b=n+2. If n>2m, the exponent (m,2)
lies below the source polygon. The inherited support theorem therefore makes
its raw coefficient zero. Extracting coefficient m from the displayed formula
forces s=0. This uses an actual source theorem, not an assumed balanced-word
identification. If n<=2m, the elementary bound s<=2m suffices instead.

Write the cubic coefficients as A,B,C,D. The polynomial certificates establish
A,C,B,D>=0, AC<=B², BD<=C² and AD<=BC for m<=n and
(n<=2m or s=0). They yield the zero-extended CrossLC property of Q. The already
checked binomial smoothing and shift adapters yield CrossLC of the literal
source row. Seven core words of length at most two are evaluated separately;
their rows are shifted nonnegative quadratics with checked coefficient gaps.
The final target theorem is horizontal_two_raw8934, in
research/MarkovSecondHorizontal8934.lean. Consult the validation manifest for
actual accepted build/replay status, rather than treating this prose as a receipt.

This argument does not establish the stronger arbitrary-word horizontal
conjecture. The cubic before binomial smoothing can fail LC for long words
with B at a core endpoint, so merely applying residual LC to every word would
be unjustified. General higher horizontal rows remain open here.

## Experiments and searches

matrix-invariants.json records 1,023 products beginning with A through length
10. All four entries passed the horizontal adjacent checks. Three simple
same-row synchronization predicates failed, so that induction route was not
used. This is finite evidence only, not a proof of horizontal LC.

polygon-words-14.json records 8,191 A--core--B words through length 14. Of
these, 253 have their entire coefficient support in the polygon specified by
their counts; 63 of those have coprime counts. No directional LC failure was
found among the 253. No family-identification or universal theorem follows
from this scan. Earlier arbitrary-word failures do not automatically survive
this stronger support requirement.

Hosted searches on 2026-10-14 retrieved these primary sources:

* [Evans–Veselov–Winn, published target](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html):
  exact target and known special-line results; no general proof retrieved.
* [Evans, Saturation of Markov Polynomials](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18333):
  the abstract reports a constructive saturation proof using snake graphs.
  Saturation is distinct from the raw log-concavity inequalities.
* [Kang–Lee–Lim, Unimodality and Cluster Algebras from Surfaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04396):
  the abstract reports unimodality and states a log-concavity conjecture for a
  different specialization. No theorem from this paper was imported into Lean.

The search supplied no universal proof of this pinned root. No historical
novelty claim is made for the second-row identity or inequality.

second-formula-check.json verifies the exact second-row formula on 2,040
words of lengths 5 through 12. It also records the non-source word A B A^16 B
with coprime counts 2/19: its residual is [0,2,14,112,190], so 196<224.
The actual source word is different; this is not a root refutation.
